label: Closed Surfaces
notes: Open by naming the chapter as the bridge from local surface geometry to global topology. The source span is printed pages 151 through 160, and the assigned notebook turns the section into a laboratory for gluing, orientation, genus, and total Gaussian curvature.

label: Closed By Identification
notes: Begin with the word closed in its topological sense, not as a drawing convention. A closed surface has no boundary after all identifications have been made. The polygon is only a construction kit; the mathematical object is the quotient surface after matched edges have been glued.

label: Boundary Pairing Ledger
notes: Treat the edge labels as data rather than ornament. Each boundary side must have exactly one partner, and the pairing must be an involution. The orientation sign records whether the arrows are opposed or aligned, while vertex orbits tell us which corners become the same point.

label: Torus Gluing
notes: Use the torus as the clean model of orientable gluing. Opposite edges are paired with compatible reversed traversal around the polygon boundary, so a consistently chosen normal direction survives after gluing. The word remembers the same information as the edge-arrow picture.

label: Klein Bottle Contrast
notes: Now change one pairing sign and keep the rest of the mental model fixed. The Klein bottle contrast is useful because the local square still looks harmless, but transporting an orientation around one loop returns the opposite choice. This is the diagnostic failure, not a drawing defect.

label: Orientation Is A Consistency Test
notes: Explain orientation as a propagation problem on small triangles. Choose a local clockwise rule, carry it across a glued edge, and continue. If the process returns to a triangle with the opposite rule, the surface is non-orientable; if it never contradicts itself, the surface is orientable.

label: Orientation Double Cover
notes: The orientation cover replaces each point by the two possible local orientation choices. On an orientable surface the two layers separate globally; on a non-orientable surface, loops that reverse orientation switch layers. This lets the class study non-orientable geometry using an orientable cover.

label: Euler Characteristic From Cells
notes: Move from pictures to counting. A polygon model supplies one face, edge pairs after gluing, and vertex orbits after corner identifications. The Euler characteristic is the signed cell count, so a purely combinatorial ledger already predicts a topological invariant of the closed surface.

label: Orientable Genus
notes: Define genus as the number of handles for connected orientable closed surfaces. The formula chi equals two minus two genus is the bridge from a gluing ledger to a classification label. Sphere, torus, and double torus give the numerical rhythm before any proof details.

label: Nonorientable Genus
notes: Contrast the handle count with the crosscap count. A connected non-orientable closed surface has Euler characteristic two minus k, where k is the number of projective-plane summands. Its orientation double cover has twice the Euler characteristic and orientable genus k minus one.

label: Gauss-Bonnet Closes The Ledger
notes: Bring the chapter back to differential geometry. Curvature is measured locally by the surface metric, but for a closed surface the total Gaussian curvature is forced by Euler characteristic. This is where local bending and global gluing data meet in one formula.

label: Curvature Can Move, Total Cannot
notes: Emphasize the difference between local curvature distribution and total curvature budget. A surface can be smoothed, dented, or parametrized differently, and the positive and negative patches may move. For a fixed closed topology, the integral remains tied to Euler characteristic.

label: Notebook Diagnostics
notes: Connect the lecture to the assigned notebook checks. The computational habit is to verify the boundary pairing involution, confirm the orientation signs, compute genus from the ledger, and compare the Euler characteristic with the total-curvature target. The pictures earn trust through these tests.

label: Takeaways
notes: Close by giving students a durable reading strategy for closed surfaces. First write the gluing data, then test orientation, then count cells to get Euler characteristic, then translate that value into genus and total curvature. The same sequence turns diagrams into accountable geometry.
